subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps

Hi Alex / Dana,

Thanks again for taking the demo today - great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the recommended model shortlist and our rationale so your engineering and ML teams can start a focused eval without chasing a long model list.

Recommended shortlist (balanced for your use case: multi-turn customer support with long context > 4k tokens):

1) rw-epic-13B-quant (recommended - latency/cost-balanced)
   - Rationale: Strong instruction-following and robust long-context handling when quantized; avg latency ~120ms/token on our Dedicated C5 class, cost ~ $25 / 1M tokens (inference only).
   - Best fit if you want predictable per-token economics and plan to use prefix caching.

2) open-vista-70B (high-quality, higher-cost)
   - Rationale: Highest quality on subtle intent/clarification cases in our evals; avg latency ~220ms/token, cost ~ $110 / 1M tokens.
   - Best fit for escalations and high-risk responses where accuracy matters more than cost.

3) rw-lite-7B (low-cost baseline)
   - Rationale: Fastest latency and cheapest; good for short-turn automations and intent classification. Latency ~80ms/token, cost ~ $8 / 1M tokens.

Attached: redwood-post-demo-slide.pdf (short slides), acme-benchmark-summary.csv (our eval run on your sample prompt set), acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (anonymized prompts we used). Full benchmark dashboard link below.

Quality/regression note: we ran the prompt set you shared (anonymized) through these three variants and included per-case regression flags in the CSV. There were 12 cases where rw-lite-7B produced unacceptable hallucinations; rw-epic-13B had 2 borderline cases, open-vista-70B had none.

Next steps we recommended on the call:
- Your team to review the attached prompt set and the CSV to prioritize the most critical cases (owner: Acme ML).
- Schedule a short SE deep-dive with Dev to validate latency on your internal infra and run a 1k-sample eval (schedule link below).
- We'll provide a provisional cost model for 12-month run rate once you confirm expected qps and caching policy.

Proposed meeting times for the SE deep-dive (30m): Mon 6/1 10:00-10:30 PT or Tue 6/2 14:00-14:30 PT - tell me which works and I'll send calendar invite.

If helpful, I can also spin up a Dedicated trial instance with rw-epic-13B quant and snapshot your 1k-sample runs next week.

Thanks, looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Alex, quick answers and next steps below.

Latency for long context (8k+):
- rw-epic-13B-quant: we see tail latencies grow roughly linearly with context length; typical observed mean-per-token remains ~120-160ms/token for 8k contexts on our Dedicated C5 infra with KV cache enabled. Worst-case 95th ~= 420ms/token for very large generations (>2k new tokens).
- open-vista-70B: mean ~220-270ms/token on same infra; 95th can be ~700ms/token for very long generations.
- rw-lite-7B: mean ~80-100ms/token.

Projected cost (very approximate) for 10M tokens/month with 40% cache hit:
- rw-epic-13B-quant: ~$150/month net inference (that number seems off? wait), sorry let me recalc - correct estimates: ~$1500 / month (post-cache).
- open-vista-70B: ~$6600 / month (post-cache).
- rw-lite-7B: ~$480 / month (post-cache).

We'll produce a detailed cost model once you confirm target qps and average generation length.

SE deep-dive: Dev can lead latency/infra validation. Lauren (Customer Success) will coordinate the mutual action plan and rollout checkpoints. Dev, can you pick an available 30m slot Mon/Tue next week and share a calendar invite?

Action items:
- Acme ML: confirm 1k-sample subset and priority cases (owner: Alex / Acme ML).
- Redwood (Marissa): provide finalized per-token cost model and an infra playbook for Dedicated trial.
- Redwood (Dev): run a quick 100-sample latency pass with your sample prompts on a Dedicated staging instance and share raw numbers.

Link to shared evals and slides: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLink/redwood-acme-evals

Thanks, I'll follow up with calendar invites and the cost worksheet.

Best,
Marissa
